subject: Re: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence checklist (HelixHealth)
messages:
From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@helixhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we evaluate a private VPC deployment with customer-managed keys, our legal and security teams have a short evidence checklist we need to close before we can sign the DPA. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the following for a private deployment (on-prem/VPC):

- Clear statement of tenant key custody and operator roles (who holds KEK/DEK, who can access keys).
- Sample audit log extract showing operator/admin actions (redacted).
- Confirmation of any remote operator break-glass process and proof of forensics retention.
- Data egress detection and prevention controls for model outputs and telemetry.
- List of subprocessors involved in the private deployment package (including any third-party monitoring/telemetry vendors).

We have attached a short DPA-request-form with the items we need (DPA-request-form.pdf).

Also include expected turnaround (we'd like these artifacts within 5 business days if possible).

Best,
Paula Mendes
Head of Security & Privacy
HelixHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence request

Hi Paula — thanks for the clear checklist and for attaching the form. We're able to provide detailed artifacts for private deployments; I'll coordinate internally and get back with a consolidated package.

Quick notes so expectations are aligned:
- For BYOK on VPC/on-prem we support customer-managed KEKs in customer KMS (BYOK flow) and can run the Redwood control plane in a customer VPC or provide a private-hosted control plane depending on your needs.
- Operator access: we can limit operator actions to a defined set and provide audit records; we do not hold customer KEKs in plaintext.
- Subprocessors: there are a few optional monitoring/telemetry connectors used for health checks in some private deployments — we'll enumerate which are used in a given package.

Ben / Karthik — can you pull together the technical checklist and a sample redacted audit log excerpt (sample_audit_log_excerpt.json)? Aim to include the privdep_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx and a short ops runbook for the key-handshake.

Paula — we'll aim to deliver the bundle by Friday (2025-03-14). If you need faster turnaround for legal review, let us know which items are highest priority.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence request — technical package

Hi Paula — attaching a consolidated technical checklist (privdep_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx) and a short ops runbook for the BYOK handshake (ops_runbook_kms-handshake.pdf). Below are answers to the specific items you listed:

1) Tenant key custody and operator roles- Custody: Customer holds the KEK in their KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or an on-prem HSM).
- Redwood generates ephemeral DEKs at model startup encrypted under the customer KEK; we never persist KEKs in plaintext.
- Operator roles: Redwood operator accounts are scoped; escalation requires an on-call approval flow and Audit 2-step approval (documented in the runbook).

2) Sample audit log excerpt- See attached sample_audit_log_excerpt.json (redacted). It shows operator actions (restart, patch, container exec) with timestamp, operator id, and justification field.

3) Break-glass process and forensics retention- Break-glass: there is a mutually agreed runbook; operator break-glass requires customer-provided OTP and an immediately recorded justification.
- Forensics: logs are retained for 90 days by default and snapshots for 14 days; longer retention customizable per contract (we can add an addendum).

4) Data egress detection/prevention- We provide content-filtering hooks and outbound egress firewall templates. For private deployments we can enable model-output watermarking and token-level leak detection hooks; telemetry is limited to heartbeat + encrypted metrics unless explicitly enabled.

5) Subprocessors- For private packages: optional monitoring agent vendor (ProbeCo), container registry (thirdparty-registry.example.com), and a managed backup vendor (StoreSafe). If you prefer no third-party telemetry, we can ship a minimal bundle with no external telemetry.

Open items for confirmation from Helix: preferred KMS provider, required retention window, whether Helix wants telemetry disabled by default.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: privdep_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx, ops_runbook_kms-handshake.pdf, sample_audit_log_excerpt.json

From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@helixhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence request — DPA redlines attached

Thanks Ben and Soojin — the artifacts look helpful. Legal attached a redlined DPA (dpa_redlines_helix_v1.docx). A few follow-ups from our side before we proceed to signature:

- We need a formal clause stating Redwood will not have access to customer KEKs and confirming the handshake flow (we proposed specific language in the redline).
- Please confirm subprocessors list in writing (ProbeCo, StoreSafe, thirdparty-registry.example.com) and whether those vendors will have any access to plaintext data.
- We request a sample SOC 2 Type II certificate or link to the report (if available) and an attestation for the private deployment configuration.
- For the audit log excerpt: can you provide a CSV extract that matches our SIEM ingestion schema (timestamp, user, action, resource, justification)?

Also, Helix requires that any operator break-glass events be notified to our security mailing list within 1 hour.

If you can confirm items above and provide the CSV audit extract and SOC 2 link by Friday, we can route the redline to procurement for initial sign-off.

Best,
Paula

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BYOK / VPC private deploy evidence request — delivery plan

Paula — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Short plan and owners: 

- Legal clause confirming non-access to KEKs and handshake language: Marissa Cole (Legal Ops) will propose final wording by Monday EOD and share an annotated DPA.
- Subprocessor attestation and list (written): Ben will produce a signed attestation listing vendors and their access scope; default private package has no plaintext access by subprocessors.
- SOC 2 and attestation: we'll provide a link to the SOC 2 Type II report (read-only access) and a short attestation for the private build.
- Audit log CSV: Ben/Karthik will export a CSV match for your SIEM schema and place it in the shared Drive folder.
- Break-glass notification: we accept the 1-hour notification requirement and will add that to the runbook; operational SLAs to be reflected in the DPA.

Deliverables we will upload to the Drive link and DocuSign envelope today: privdep_evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx, sample_audit_log_excerpt.json (and CSV), ops_runbook_kms-handshake.pdf, signed_subprocessor_attestation.pdf, link to SOC2.

If Helix wants an interactive technical call to walk through the audit extract and runbook, Ben and Karthik are available Monday morning PT. Otherwise we'll send the package and updated redline for procurement review.

Thanks — Soojin
